text:
Agent: Thank you for calling the exchange support line, my name is Karen. How can I help you today?
Customer: Hi, yes. I'm trying to place a limit order on the ETH perpetual, and it keeps getting rejected. The error says insufficient margin, but I have like four thousand dollars in my futures wallet.
Agent: I'm sorry about that. Let me look. Could you give me your user ID?
Customer: Sure, it's eight-eight-one, four-four-two-zero.
Agent: Thank you. I see here you currently have two open positions in cross margin mode, one on SOL and one on BTC, and both are in a loss. So your available margin is much lower than your wallet balance.
Customer: Oh. Okay. Um, so the wallet shows total, but not available.
Agent: Exactly. The unrealized loss is eating into your available balance. Also your leverage on the ETH order is set to fifty x, which requires a larger initial margin buffer at that size.
Customer: Fifty x? I didn't set that. Oh wait, I think it defaulted when I switched the pair.
Agent: It can carry over. I'd suggest lowering it to five or ten x. You can do that on the order panel, top right, next to the pair name.
Customer: Okay, I see it. Let me try ten. And, um, should I switch to isolated margin?
Agent: That could protect your other positions, yes. Just be aware that you'll need to allocate margin manually to each position.
Customer: Got it. Thanks, it went through now.
Agent: Wonderful. Is there anything else?
Customer: No, that's all. Thanks.
